records.name: Castilla-La Mancha
records.summary: Not individually flagged by the country dossier in any respect: no region-specific law, incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified for this region either way (and it is not one of the regions the dossier's legislative-inventory note enumerates). The national position therefore governs: no facility, expression or assembly restriction exists at sub-national level anywhere in the country, the 2023 national trans-equality law is implemented by the regional government, and the national victimisation baseline applies - a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The dossier's general notes place this region in the sparsely-populated interior where LGBT-visible community life is thinner than in the big cities.

records.name: Cantabria
records.summary:
Under Spain's Law 4/2023, gazette-published, the administrative and education-facing provisions of the national trans-equality law are implemented by the autonomous communities — Cantabria's government among them; the 2023 gender-recognition reform (self-declaration from age 12, no medical diagnosis) drew an international rights body to place the country among autonomy-first jurisdictions.

The surviving record contains no Cantabrian statute, ordinance, enforcement series or incident finding; the region's relevance to a visitor lies in implementation posture under the same national framework, not in separate restriction.

records.name: Andalucía
records.summary: Direction: better than the national position - the oldest and deepest regional framework in Spain. Ley 2/2014, an integral law for non-discrimination on grounds of gender identity, was among the first trans-specific regional laws in Europe; Ley 8/2017 of 28 December (in force 4 February 2018) guarantees LGTBI rights and equal treatment for LGTBI people and their families; and the regional government approved an equality strategy for 2024-2028 on 26 December 2024. Visitor-relevant geography: Andalucía carries much of Spain's LGBTQ mass tourism (Mijas, Torremolinos, Seville), which coexists with school-content opt-out ('pin parental') conflicts that historically concentrated in Andalusian municipalities.

records.name: Chaco
records.summary:
No Chaco-specific trans statute, quota-compliance finding or enforcement series survives in the record. The framework is national: a April 2025 national feature described the trans community facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' after decree roll-back of the Gender Identity Law, and a national hate-crime observatory reported 227 SOGI-motivated hate crimes for 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, its highest decade count, one every 38 hours, most attackers security-force personnel or unidentified — a baseline applying across the provinces including this one.

Visitor exposure in Chaco therefore tracks the national position: no provincial criminalisation survives in the record, amid a documented national surge in anti-trans violence and a contested federal law.
